```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(readxl)
library(multcomp)
library(onewaytests)
library(car) 
library(emmeans)
library(writexl)
```

#Reading in the Data
``` {r reading in the data and cleaning names}
raw_data_all_expts <- read_xlsx("Compiled Data - 1_5_2026.xlsx")

cleaned_data <- raw_data_all_expts %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  mutate(dose = factor(dose, levels = c("Vehicle Control", "10 mM TCA", "Solvent Control", "5 mM TCEOH")),
         strain = factor(strain, levels = c("N2", "BZ555", "UA44")),
         experiment = factor(experiment),
         day = factor(day)
         )

long_data <- cleaned_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("rep"),
    names_to = "replicate",
    values_to = "eggs"
  )

egg_counts <- long_data %>%
  group_by(strain, dose, day, eggs) %>%
  summarise(n_worms = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

``` {r split by control / treatment type - raw data}
tca_raw_data <- long_data %>%
  filter(dose %in% c("Vehicle Control", "10 mM TCA")) %>%
  mutate(worm_id = paste(experiment, strain, dose, day, replicate, sep = "_"),
         dose = relevel(dose, ref = "Vehicle Control"),
         day = relevel(day, ref = "1"),
         strain = relevel(strain, ref = "N2"))

tceoh_raw_data <- long_data %>%
  filter(dose %in% c("Solvent Control", "5 mM TCEOH")) %>%
  mutate(worm_id = paste(experiment, strain, dose, day, replicate, sep = "_"),
         dose = relevel(dose, ref = "Solvent Control"),
         day = relevel(day, ref = "1"),
         strain = relevel(strain, ref = "N2"))
```

#Three Way ANOVAs - Raw Data
``` {r running a three-way ANOVA - raw data normalized - TCA}
#Running an ANOVA with all of the compounds being normalized to their respective controls (vehicle or solvent control)
tca_raw_model <- aov(eggs ~ day * dose * strain, data = tca_raw_data)

summary(tca_raw_model)
#Strain difference

#Checking the normality of the residuals - data meets the normality assumption
res <- residuals(tca_raw_model)
qqnorm(res)
qqline(res)
hist(res)

#Levene's Test of ANOVA model to check assumption of equal variances, but ultimately central limit theorem should be fine here.
leveneTest(eggs ~ day * dose * strain, 
           data = tca_raw_data,
           center = median)
```

``` {r running a three-way ANOVA - raw data normalized - TCEOH}
#Running an ANOVA with all of the compounds being normalized to their respective controls (vehicle or solvent control)
tceoh_raw_model <- aov(eggs ~ day * dose * strain, data = tceoh_raw_data)

summary(tceoh_raw_model)
#day, dose, strain, day:dose, dose:strain are all significant

#Checking the normality of the residuals - data meets the normality assumption
res <- residuals(tceoh_raw_model)
qqnorm(res)
qqline(res)
hist(res)

#Levene's Test of ANOVA model to check assumption of equal variances, but ultimately central limit theorem should be fine here.
leveneTest(eggs ~ day * dose * strain, 
           data = tceoh_raw_data,
           center = median)
```

``` {r running a robust ANOVA - raw data, eval = FALSE}
library(afex)
#Using this package's ANOVA to see if applying a heteroskedascity correction changes things a lot.

tca_raw_robust <- aov_ez(
  id = "worm_id",   # whatever identifies worms
  dv = "eggs",
  between = c("day", "dose", "strain"),
  data = tca_raw_data,
  type = 3,
  white.adjust = TRUE
)

summary(tca_raw_robust)
#p-values do not change between the two models, still the same

tceoh_raw_robust <- aov_ez(
  id = "worm_id",   # whatever identifies worms
  dv = "eggs",
  between = c("day", "dose", "strain"),
  data = tceoh_raw_data,
  type = 3,
  white.adjust = TRUE
)

summary(tceoh_raw_robust)
#Same exact p-values as the first model, no change in the results
```

``` {r summary tables - raw data}
tca_raw_table <- summary(tca_raw_model)
tceoh_raw_table <- summary(tceoh_raw_model)
```

#Plotting - Raw Data
``` {r plotting data}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Summarize normalized data for plotting
plot_raw_data <- long_data %>%
  group_by(strain, day, dose) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_eggs = mean(eggs, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_eggs = sd(eggs, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    se_eggs = sd_eggs / sqrt(n)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

``` {r line plot for trends over days option 2}
# Line Plot - trends across days per dose and per strain
ggplot(plot_raw_data, aes(x = day, y = mean_eggs, color = dose, group = dose)) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.35), shape = 16) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.35), size = 1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_eggs - se_eggs, ymax = mean_eggs + se_eggs),
                width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.35), size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap( ~ strain) +
  labs(title = "Trends of Normalized Eggs in Utero Across Days", x = "Day", y = "Percent Control of Eggs in Utero", color = "Dose") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +   # Prism-like color palette
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = c(1, 2)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90"), # light grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

#Normalizing within Controls
``` {r normalizing within control}
normalized_by_control <- long_data %>%
  group_by(experiment, strain, day) %>%
  mutate(
    vehicle_mean = mean(eggs[dose == "Vehicle Control"], na.rm = TRUE),
    solvent_mean = mean(eggs[dose == "Solvent Control"], na.rm = TRUE),

    control_mean = case_when(
      dose %in% c("Vehicle Control", "10 mM TCA") ~ vehicle_mean,
      dose %in% c("Solvent Control", "5 mM TCEOH") ~ solvent_mean,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    percent_control = (eggs / control_mean) * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

``` {r split by control / treatment type - normalized data}
tca_normalized_data <- normalized_by_control %>%
  filter(dose %in% c("Vehicle Control", "10 mM TCA")) %>%
  mutate(worm_id = paste(experiment, strain, dose, day, replicate, sep = "_"),
         dose = relevel(dose, ref = "Vehicle Control"),
         day = relevel(day, ref = "1"),
         strain = relevel(strain, ref = "N2"))

tceoh_normalized_data <- normalized_by_control %>%
  filter(dose %in% c("Solvent Control", "5 mM TCEOH")) %>%
  mutate(worm_id = paste(experiment, strain, dose, day, replicate, sep = "_"),
         dose = relevel(dose, ref = "Solvent Control"),
         day = relevel(day, ref = "1"),
         strain = relevel(strain, ref = "N2"))
```

#Three Way ANOVAs - Normalized Data
``` {r running a three-way ANOVA - normalized by control data - TCA}
#Running an ANOVA with all of the compounds being normalized to their respective controls (vehicle or solvent control)
tca_model <- aov(percent_control ~ day * dose * strain, data = tca_normalized_data)

summary(tca_model)
#Nothing is significant

#Checking the normality of the residuals - data meets the normality assumption
res <- residuals(tca_model)
qqnorm(res)
qqline(res)
hist(res)

#Levene's Test of ANOVA model to check assumption of equal variances, but ultimately central limit theorem should be fine here. Probably significant bcause I percent control everything so the variance for the control is tighter.
leveneTest(percent_control ~ day * dose * strain, 
           data = tca_normalized_data,
           center = median)
```

``` {r running a three-way ANOVA - normalized by control data - TCEOH}
#Running an ANOVA with all of the compounds being normalized to their respective controls (vehicle or solvent control)
tceoh_model <- aov(percent_control ~ day * dose * strain, data = tceoh_normalized_data)

summary(tceoh_model)
#All factors are significant

#Checking the normality of the residuals - data meets the normality assumption
res <- residuals(tceoh_model)
qqnorm(res)
qqline(res)
hist(res)

#Levene's Test of ANOVA model to check assumption of equal variances, but ultimately central limit theorem should be fine here. Probably significant bcause I percent control everything so the variance for the control is tighter.
leveneTest(percent_control ~ day * dose * strain, 
           data = tceoh_normalized_data,
           center = median)
```

``` {r running a robust ANOVA - normalized data, eval = FALSE}
library(afex)
#Using this package's ANOVA to see if applying a heteroskedascity correction changes things a lot.

tca_model_robust <- aov_ez(
  id = "worm_id",   # whatever identifies worms
  dv = "percent_control",
  between = c("day", "dose", "strain"),
  data = tca_normalized_data,
  type = 3,
  white.adjust = TRUE
)

summary(tceoh_model_robust)
#Nothing is significant still. p-values do not change between the two models.

tceoh_model_robust <- aov_ez(
  id = "worm_id",   # whatever identifies worms
  dv = "percent_control",
  between = c("day", "dose", "strain"),
  data = tceoh_normalized_data,
  type = 3,
  white.adjust = TRUE
)

summary(tceoh_model_robust)
#Everything is significant, same exact p-values as the first model.

#Since nothing changes, I will use the simpler ANOVA model.
```

``` {r summary tables - normalized data}
tca_table <- summary(tca_model)
tceoh_table <- summary(tceoh_model)
```

#Investigating TCEOH Model - Normalized Data
``` {r estimated marginal means}
library(emmeans)
emmeans(tceoh_model, pairwise ~ day | strain * dose, adjust = "none") 
#Here no multiple comparisons are being made, safe to leave unadjusted

emmeans(tceoh_model, pairwise ~ strain | day * dose, adjust = "tukey")
#multiple comparisons are being made, using Tukey's

emmeans(tceoh_model, pairwise ~ dose | day * strain, adjust = "none")
#Here no multiple comparisons are being made, safe to leave unadjusted
```

``` {r split data by dose}
solv_ctrl_only <- tceoh_normalized_data %>%
  filter(dose == "Solvent Control")

tceoh_only <- tceoh_normalized_data %>%
  filter(dose == "5 mM TCEOH")
```

``` {r Two-Way ANOVAs, eval = FALSE}
#Running a two-way ANOVA within the dose
solv_only_model <- aov(percent_control ~ day * strain, data = solv_ctrl_only)

summary(solv_only_model)
#Nothing is significant

#Checking the normality of the residuals - data meets the normality assumption
res <- residuals(solv_only_model)
qqnorm(res)
qqline(res)
hist(res)

#Levene's Test of ANOVA model to check assumption of equal variances, but ultimately central limit theorem should be fine here. Probably significant bcause I percent control everything so the variance for the control is tighter.
leveneTest(percent_control ~ day * strain, 
           data = solv_ctrl_only,
           center = median)

tceoh_only_model <- aov(percent_control ~ day * strain, data = tceoh_only)

summary(tceoh_only_model)
#Everything is significant

#Checking the normality of the residuals - data meets the normality assumption
res <- residuals(tceoh_only_model)
qqnorm(res)
qqline(res)
hist(res)

#Levene's Test of ANOVA model to check assumption of equal variances, but ultimately central limit theorem should be fine here. Probably significant bcause I percent control everything so the variance for the control is tighter.
leveneTest(percent_control ~ day * strain, 
           data = tceoh_only,
           center = median)

#If I'm using estimated marginal means, not necessary to do two-way ANOVA but good to still check.
```

#Export Stats
``` {r exporting all relevant stats}
library(writexl)

tidy_anova <- function(model) {
  summary(model)[[1]] %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    mutate(term = trimws(term))
}

anova_tca_raw    <- tidy_anova(tca_raw_model)
anova_tceoh_raw  <- tidy_anova(tceoh_raw_model)
anova_tca_norm   <- tidy_anova(tca_model)
anova_tceoh_norm <- tidy_anova(tceoh_model)

emm_day_tceoh_contrasts    <- as.data.frame(emmeans(tceoh_model, pairwise ~ day | strain * dose)$contrasts)
emm_strain_tceoh_contrasts <- as.data.frame(emmeans(tceoh_model, pairwise ~ strain | day * dose, adjust = "tukey")$contrasts)
emm_dose_tceoh_contrasts   <- as.data.frame(emmeans(tceoh_model, pairwise ~ dose | day * strain)$contrasts)

write_xlsx(
  list(
    anova_tca_raw     = anova_tca_raw,
    anova_tceoh_raw   = anova_tceoh_raw,
    anova_tca_norm    = anova_tca_norm,
    anova_tceoh_norm  = anova_tceoh_norm,
    emm_day_tceoh     = emm_day_tceoh_contrasts,
    emm_strain_tceoh  = emm_strain_tceoh_contrasts,
    emm_dose_tceoh    = emm_dose_tceoh_contrasts
  ),
  "eggs_in_utero_stats.xlsx"
)
```
